Now I can see the issue clearly. The error message shows:

```
[('url', 'https%3A//twitter.com/Twitter/status/266367358078169089')] != [('url', 'https://twitter.com/Twitter/status/266367358078169089')]
```

The URL is being double-encoded:
- The cassette expects: `https%3A//twitter.com/...` (which is `https://twitter.com/...` URL-encoded once)
- But the request is sending: `https%253A%2F%2Ftwitter.com/...` (which is `https%3A%2F%2Ftwitter.com/...` URL-encoded again)

The `%253A` is the double-encoded version of `:`, and `%2F` is the double-encoded version of `/`.

Looking at the URL in the error:
- Expected: `https://twitter.com/Twitter/status/266367358078169089`
- Got: `https%253A%2F%2Ftwitter.com%2FTwitter%2Fstatus%2F266367358078169089`

Wait, let me re-read this more carefully. The error says:
- Request has: `https%253A%2F%2Ftwitter.com%2FTwitter%2Fstatus%2F266367358078169089`
- Cassette has: `https%3A%2F%2Ftwitter.com%2FTwitter%2Fstatus%2F266367358078169089`

So the request is sending a double-encoded URL, while the cassette expects a single-encoded URL.

The issue is that the `url` parameter value is already a URL (`https://twitter.com/...`), and when it's passed to `requests` as a query parameter, `requests` automatically URL-encodes it. However, something in the code is pre-encoding it before passing it to `requests`, causing double encoding.
